name: MSA Safety
headline: Maker of certified life-safety gear, such as breathing apparatus and gas detectors, that firefighters standardize on.
what_short: Safety gear: gas detectors, breathing apparatus
what_it_does: MSA Safety makes gas and flame detectors, breathing apparatus for fire services, and protective gear such as hard hats. Its 2025 sales were about $1.9 billion. Its products are certified to safety standards, and the Americas region carries about 80% of its segment profit.
why_it_passed: Customers buy certified life-safety devices and a fire department standardizes on one breathing-apparatus platform and trains on it, so they do not switch on price.
It earns about 53% a year before tax on the operating capital it needs, a figure that has stayed between 41% and 53% for nearly a decade.
Operating margin rose from 14.3% in 2016 to 19.8% in 2025, with gross margin at 46.5%.
Rivals with deep pockets did not win: Honeywell wrote down and sold its protective equipment business, and 3M bought a business instead of building one.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $84.50 to $137.29 against a price of $180.71, above the top of the range. A buyer at that price would expect about 4.5% a year, or 3.7% with half the growth, less than a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.60%).
watch: It still has product-liability claims from past cumulative-trauma cases, about 21,372 claims at mid-2026 with no reserve set aside, and defense costs are expensed as they arise.
Net debt is $954.7 million after buying Autronica, about 2.0 times adjusted earnings before interest, tax and depreciation.
The International segment earns only a 15.2% margin against 28.9% in the Americas.
